_role: Clause 1 of the publish bar. GENERATED by record_bar_evidence.py from the blind seat records that reviewed this exact commit — never hand-written. The bar re-derives the tallies from the same seats, so editing this file does not move the verdict.

p1s.summary: The outgoing reference list's year, title, volume, pages and DOI are hand-typed and bound to no fetch record — only the author segment, the journal name and the PMID-to-superscript pairing are guarded. The entries are all correct today (all 24 checked field-by-field against the deposited records), but an ordinary edit — retyping a year, adding an entry, fixing a page range — would silently break one and nothing would go red. The sibling manuscript has exactly this guard and this one does not, so the pair is inverted.
p1s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md lines 34-36 say so in its own banner. test_journal_references_match_the_prose.py opens only the article and the references file (lines 37-38) plus aso/journal-reference-authors.json for the author segment (line 148); test_each_entry_carries_the_pmid_its_citation_names compares the entry's 'PMID: N' against the article's own <!--PMID:N--> comment, both sides typed in this repository. lint_citations.py anchors an identifier only by requiring the string to appear in some tracked .json, so swapping a real DOI for a different real tracked DOI would pass. The counterpart guard is research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_endpoint_reference_list_binds_to_what_was_fetched.py.

p1s.summary: Nothing binds the paper to disclose a named reagent's exact 16/16 genomic matches, so a re-run that gave one to the other reagent would change no prose and redden no gate. The aggregate pair (156/135) and the 'does not separate them' verb are bound; no assertion connects per_design exact_sites for a named reagent to anything the article says. The article does report that reagent's TWO-MISMATCH genome-arm site, so the disclosure of one class of per-site genome finding is prose held by nothing while its sibling class is not disclosed at all.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_numbered_claims_no_instrument_read.py::test_the_two_genome_wide_loads_are_the_genome_screens_own; research/modalities/tests/test_aso_genome_offtarget.py tests the artifact's own structure; a scoped git grep over both test directories finds no assertion joining per_design[…]['exact_sites'] for a named reagent to article prose

p1s.summary: The scope repair on the fifth screen — 'unambiguous GRCh38' — is bound by no guard, and the wording it replaced still stands in three deposited files, so an ordinary edit reverting it would go green. The repair itself is real and correct: 4.88% of genome windows carry an N and are not scanned.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/aso-genome-offtarget.json: denominator.windows_total 3099747808, windows_with_N 151138112, windows_scanned 2948609696, n_fraction 0.0488. A guard search over every test that opens fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md (29 files) returns only two that mention GRCh38/mitochondrial/unambiguous, and in both the string appears in a docstring or in an assertion about the 156/135 pair — neither touches the scope word. test_genomics_prose_matches_the_screen_artifacts.py DOES bind windows_with_N, but its PAPER constant (line 35) is aso/fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md, not the journal article.

p1s.summary: The Abstract's statement of how much of the OSWG framework this work executes is read by no guard. The scope claim is bound in exactly one place, whose site anchor matches only the Introduction sentence; the Abstract carries an independent statement of the same scope that no site pattern reaches, and the abstract guard requires only two universal needles. So the abstract's framework claim could be widened to any of the six phrasings the Introduction forbids and every gate would stay green.

p1s.summary: The assumed replicate SD 0.35 reaches the page at exactly one site and no guard reads it, so an edit to it silently desynchronises the two power figures that ARE guarded.
p1s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md line 323 is the only occurrence of 0.35 in the article. The producing constant is SIGMA = 0.35 at research/manuscripts/aso_falsification_power.py:43. The guard test_the_falsification_power_figures_are_derived_not_typed (research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py:452-483) binds only the OUTPUTS — its two regexes capture the power percentages, TRUE_SELECTIVITY and the three void SDs, never 0.35. Measured consequence: prose SD 0.45 would make the printed 'about 80%/30%' actually 60.9%/21.3%, and every guard stays green.

p1s.summary: The interval's sidedness is unbound, and it moves all three void thresholds by about 45%.
p1s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md line 326, 'the upper limit of a two-sided 95% interval below 5'. A scoped git grep for 'two-sided|one-sided|sided 95' over research/manuscripts/tests research/modalities/tests scripts/tests returns no test reading this article. The void regex at test_journal_article_numbers.py:99 contains neither 'two-sided' nor '95%'. Recomputed: a copy-edit to 'one-sided' makes the correct void SDs 0.955 / 1.956 / 2.776 against the printed 0.65 / 1.53 / 2.25, and nothing fails.

p1s.summary: The falsification cut is stated at two sites and only one is pinned — the one-of-a-pair gap, in the sentence whose own guard message names that exact risk.
p1s.evidence: test_the_falsification_cut_is_the_stated_value (research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_paper_states_what_its_own_claims_depend_on.py:216) asserts re.search(r'cut of 5\.0', text), pinning article line 321. The second statement of the same constant, line 326's 'interval below 5', is read by nothing — a scoped grep for 'interval below|below 5' over the three test directories returns rc=1. Changing that site alone to 'below 4' makes the void SD at three replicates 0.558 rather than the printed 0.65, and the paper self-contradictory, with every gate green.
